title: Whole-body Mass Spectrometry Imaging by Infrared Matrix-assisted Laser Desorption Electrospray Ionization (IR-MALDESI)
protocol: Prepare an isopentane/dry ice bath by placing ~200 ml of isopentane in a clean beaker inside a secondary container of dry ice in a fume hood.
Euthanize 2-day-old whole neonatal mouse pup by Avertin overdose (7.5 mg/g body weight).
Freeze the tissue in the isopentane/dry ice bath to preserve tissue structure.
Place and remove the mouse pup in cryomold from the isopentane/dry ice bath using a pre-cleaned pair of forceps.
Store the flash-frozen tissue at -80 °C until analysis.
Apply a layer of optimal cutting temperature (OCT) mounting medium to a 40 mm cryostat specimen disc.
Gently place the frozen whole mouse onto the OCT coated specimen holder to adhere mouse to the disc in the desired orientation for sectioning.
Place the disc (with OCT and tissue section) on Peltier sample holder in cryostat and press Peltier power button.
Wait 10 min for sample to come to thermal equilibrium.
Slice the tissue into sections of the desired thickness at -20 °C using the rotary microtome housed inside the cryostat.
Use the anti-roll glass plate to prevent the sliced tissue section from rolling.
Use the cryostat vacuum hose and brushes to remove unwanted tissue debris.
Once the tissue is sectioned, use the blade guard to cover the sharp microtome blade to avoid personal injuries.
Orient mouse section on the specimen plate and thaw-mount onto a pre-cleaned glass microscope slide by bringing the slide as close as possible to the tissue section, without touching it.
Turn on the mid-IR laser and launch the laser control application on the computer.
Choose the desired wavelength using the laser control application supplied by the manufacturer.
Turn on the stage controller, launch the custom user control program (RASTIR), and calibrate the stage position using the home button.
Prepare electrospray solution typically with a 50:50 (v/v) methanol/water with 0.2% formic acid for positive-ion mode.
Select the electrospray solvent composition according to the experiment, such as 5 mM ammonium hydroxide for negative-ion mode imaging applications.
Use 1 mM acetic acid as the modifier for polarity switching IR-MALDESI MSI.
Fill a 1 ml syringe with electrospray solvent and flush the silica capillary with new solvent.
Align ESI emitter on axis with MS inlet using optimized source parameters.
Start the electrospray and evaluate its stability by monitoring the total ion current (TIC) for >10 min.
Turn off the electrospray before placing the sample on the stage.
Place the thaw-mounted tissue onto the IR-MALDESI sample plate within the camera view.
Make sure hands are clear of the ESI emitter.
Restart the electrospray.
Close the access door of the IR-MALDESI source.
Purge enclosure with dry nitrogen to prevent condensation of water on the surface of the tissue.
Turn on the DC power supply (~12 V) to the Peltier plate to cool the sample plate.
Cool the stage to -9 °C and allow the mounted tissue to come to thermal equilibrium (~5-10 min).
Stop nitrogen purge.
Expose the tissue to ambient relative humidity by opening the source access door.
Place a beaker of warm water inside the enclosure if the lab's relative humidity is below 10-15%.
Close the access door and restart the flow of dry nitrogen to reduce the relative humidity to 10±2%.
Adjust the nitrogen flow rate empirically to maintain a constant layer of ice throughout the experiment.
Move the stage to the analysis position using the "LASER position" button in RASTIR GUI.
Use the adjustment diode of the laser to ensure an off-tissue region will be ablated.
Fire a laser shot in an off-tissue region to calibrate the laser offset with respect to camera view.
Click the "Laser Test Fire" button to update the laser position.
Return to "CAMERA position" and update the laser position by placing the laser alignment reticle on the laser ablation spot.
Click the ROI button and adjust the size and position of ROI for the tissue section being analyzed.
Input appropriate experimental parameters such as step size in X and Y directions (in mm).
Name the MSI file in the "Project Name" box.
Include a portion of off-tissue that serves as control when drawing an ROI.
Use the off-tissue section for peak picking.
Select the appropriate laser frequency from the dropdown box.
Input the number of laser pulses per voxel (integer values).
Set the delay between the laser trigger and mass spectrometer signal acquisition.
Locate the laser spot using the RASTIR Scan Control program.
Draw an ROI on the sample for analysis.
Choose the stage step size in millimeters.
Name the file to be saved.
Input the correct number of pulses per voxel along with the desired repetition rate.
Check the list for imaging and MS setup parameters.
Select ionization mode in mass spectrometer software.
Set electrospray voltage in mass spectrometer software.
Define solvent flow rate in mass spectrometer software.
Adjust capillary temperature in mass spectrometer software.
Specify injection time in mass spectrometer software.
Place the MS in "handshake" mode for synchronization.
Start MS acquisition.
Using RASTIR imaging software, verify all steps in checklist are completed by checking boxes.
Load the program.
Press Run to start MSI signal acquisition.
Stop mass spectrometer acquisition upon completion of the imaging experiment.
Place the instrument in standby mode.
Turn off nitrogen purge to the enclosure.
Turn off power supply to Peltier plate.
Turn off the stage controller and laser.
Open the access door.
Remove the electrospray emitter tip from inside the source enclosure using protective gloves.
Remove the extended heated metal MS inlet using protective gloves.
Wear gloves and safety goggles.
Clean the extended metal capillary inlet by ultrasonic bath in 15% nitric acid for 10 min.
Rinse the capillary inlet in HPLC-grade water for 10 min.
Rinse the capillary inlet in HPLC-grade methanol for 10 min.
Dry the metal capillary inlet under a stream of nitrogen.
Reinsert the cleaned capillary inlet into MS.
Dispose solvent in appropriate waste containers afterward.
Use the peak picking function to generate a list of tissue-specific m/z values using user-defined criteria.
